title: Nue Kua: Repairing the Heavens
subtitle: A tradition transmitted through Werner's synthesis

repair.author: E. T. C. Werner (modern compiler and author)
repair.translator: not applicable; authored in English by E. T. C. Werner
repair.locator: Chapter III · Cosmogony-p'an Ku and the Creation Myth; Chapter III · Cosmogony-p'an Ku and the Creation Myth, normalized characters 8882-9269
repair.excerpt: The pillars of Heaven were broken and the corners of the earth gave way. Hereupon Nue Kua melted stones of the five colours to repair the heavens, and cut off the feet of the tortoise to set upright the four extremities of the earth. [7] Gathering the ashes of reeds she stopped the flooding waters, and thus rescued the land of Chi, Chi Chou [the early seat of the Chinese sovereignty].
repair.note: Quotation from E. T. C. Werner's 1922 English synthesis; it is not a direct translation of the ancient source it discusses.

narrativeBlocks.title: A damaged cosmos
narrativeBlocks.body: Werner's 1922 synthesis attributes to Ssu-ma Cheng an account in which Kung Kung's rebellion ends with a mountain struck down and the cosmic supports broken.

narrativeBlocks.title: Repair after the collapse
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from the cited English edition (whitespace normalized): “The pillars of Heaven were broken and the corners of the earth gave way. Hereupon Nue Kua melted stones of the five colours to repair the heavens, and cut off the feet of the tortoise to set upright the four extremities of the earth. [7] Gathering the ashes of reeds she stopped the flooding waters, and thus rescued the land of Chi, Chi Chou [the early seat of the Chinese sovereignty].”

narrativeBlocks.title: Stones, tortoise, and reeds
narrativeBlocks.body: In the account Werner quotes, Nue Kua melts five-coloured stones to repair heaven, uses a tortoise's feet to support earth, and stops floodwater with reed ashes.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep the transmission visible
narrativeBlocks.body: The lesson quotes Werner's English rendering of an account he attributes to Ssu-ma Cheng. It is not a direct translation made here from the Historical Records, and Werner's wording and framing should remain visible.

narrativeBlocks.title: Restoration is the central action
narrativeBlocks.body: This version centers repair after damage rather than presenting Nue Kua as the sole maker of heaven and earth.
